findings.title: immediateDelete cancels at SendGrid but never records cancellation
findings.body: When immediateDelete is true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder POSTs a SendGrid batch cancel and returns without setting cancelled or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. Reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts) and workflow/step deletion (workflows.tsx) pass immediateDelete: true. A failed cancel — including the 100 pending-cancellation cap this PR exists to avoid — is only logged, so cancelled stays unset and the cron never retries; the email is still sent. A successful cancel of a far-future batch also parks a pending cancellation until the original send time, which is exactly what fills that cap. Those callers should mark cancelled (and let the cron cancel within the hour) or, on immediate cancel, delete the row and fall back to cancelled=true if SendGrid fails.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation is not awaited before the handler returns
findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are fired inside forEach and never awaited (same pattern in handleNewBooking.ts around the reschedule loop and in bookings.tsx requestReschedule). The new design depends on the cancelled=true write (or the Twilio/SendGrid call) finishing before the API route returns. On serverless the process can freeze after the response, so the flag is never committed, the cron does not cancel the batch, and the reminder email/SMS is still delivered. The try/catch in handleNewBooking also cannot see those rejections because forEach does not await the promises.

findings.title: Cron deletes due reminders before cancelling them at SendGrid
findings.body: The job first deleteMany's every EMAIL WorkflowReminder with scheduledDate <= now, then only SendGrid-cancels rows still marked cancelled whose scheduledDate is within the next hour. A cancelled reminder whose send time has just passed (late or missed 15-minute run, or a send inside the cron interval) is removed from the database without POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends status=cancel. SendGrid still has the batch and delivers the email for the cancelled or rescheduled booking. Past-due cancelled rows need a SendGrid cancel before they are deleted.

findings.title: One SendGrid cancel error aborts the rest of the batch
findings.body: The cancel loop awaits each SendGrid request inside a single try, and only after the whole loop does it Promise.all the queued deletes. If any request throws (null referenceId, already-cancelled batch, or the pending-cancellation cap), the catch logs and exits: later reminders in that run are not cancelled, and deletes already pushed for earlier successful cancels never run. Those rows stay cancelled=true and will be retried, but a persistent error on one row blocks every subsequent reminder in the same cron invocation, so those emails still go out. Each reminder should be cancelled and deleted independently, and rows with no referenceId should be deleted without calling SendGrid.
